**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limits page | | **Seat‑belt & Child‑Safety** | • All occupants must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child‑safety seat or booster.
• The “no‑seat‑belt” law applies to all drivers and passengers. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held use while driving is prohibited (unless using a hands‑free system).
• Texting while driving is illegal. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21 (BAC 0.02% or higher).
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Yield to emergency vehicles” when lights are flashing. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **School Bus Rules** | • Vehicles must stop when a school bus is loading/unloading children.
• No passing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers.
• Keep a safe following distance. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Parking Regulations** | • No parking in front of driveways, fire hydrants, or on sidewalks.
• Pay attention to posted signs for time‑limited or permit‑only parking. | TxDOT Parking & Signage Guidelines | | **Vehicle Registration & Inspection** | • All vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Most vehicles require an annual safety inspection. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing is allowed only if the vehicle is unsafe or abandoned.
• Towing companies must follow Texas towing regulations. | Texas Transportation Code §545.021 | | **Special Situations** | • **High‑way HOV lanes**: Only vehicles with 2+ occupants or electric vehicles.
• **Construction zones**: Follow posted speed limits and detour signs. | TxDOT Construction Zone Guidelines | --- ### How to Get the Full Legal Text 1. **Texas Transportation Code** – The primary source for all traffic laws. *Website:* https://statutes.capitol.texas.gov/Docs/TS/htm/TS.545.htm 2. **TxDOT – Traffic Safety** – Offers summaries, infographics, and safety campaigns. *Website:* https://www.txdot.gov/traffic-safety.html 3. **TxDMV – Driver Handbook** – Practical guide for drivers, including licensing and registration. *Website:* https://www.txdmv.gov/handbooks 4. **Local County Courts** – For specific case law or recent rulings, check the county court’s website or the Texas Courts website. *Website:* https://www.txcourts.gov/ --- ### Quick Tips for Safe Driving in Texas - **Always keep your seat belt fastened** – it’s a legal requirement and saves lives. - **Avoid distractions** – no texting, no handheld calls. - **Observe speed limits** – they’re posted clearly; obey them. - **Respect school buses** – stop and wait until the bus resumes motion. - **Use turn signals** – give other drivers clear intent. - **Stay alert for construction zones** – speeds may drop to 25–35 mph. --- If you need details on a specific law (e.g., DUI penalties, parking restrictions in a particular city, or how to register a vehicle), let me know and I can dive deeper!
